_comment: Real (model proposed, museum returned) pairs, captured 2026-08-04 by asking the live Art Institute API about works from `phase_one_proposals.json` and recording what actually came back. `same_work` is ground truth, assigned by READING each pair as a cataloguer would -- never by running `title_key`/`artist_key` over it, which would score the comparison against its own opinion and make the corpus incapable of catching a change in it. That fixture holds model output only, so it can measure phase 1 against phase 1 and cannot reach this comparison at all; this one is the other side of the seam.

pairs.note: Exact agreement on both fields. The shape every resolution takes.

THE SAME WORK UNDER A REVERSED NAME. The museum files the artist family-name-first; the model wrote it given-name-first. Same person, same print. A comparison that reads a name as an ordered string refuses this and loses a real resolution.

pairs.note: SAME TITLE, DIFFERENT ARTIST -- the case that forces disqualification rather than deduction. The museum really does hold a 'The Great Oak', by an etcher who is not Ruisdael. Rank by relevance and this is a confident wrong answer.
Same artist, different work. Harder than a wrong-artist miss because the artist agrees, so only the title can refuse it.
